items.title: Both inverse types of a map with a quasi-inverse are contractible

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 319-321 (book Lemma 4.2.9): if a map f : A to B has a quasi-inverse, then both the type of left inverses of f and the type of right inverses of f are contractible. The statement is a contractibility claim about two auxiliary types, and the proof (source lines 322-328) has to recognise each of them as the fibre of a pre- or postcomposition map over the identity, which needs function extensionality, then to show that those composition maps are equivalences, which is where the cited results on composition of equivalences, on equivalences versus isomorphisms and on half adjoint equivalences are used, and finally to invoke the contractibility of fibres of equivalences. The identification of the two inverse types with those fibres is the whole reduction and it is absent from the statement.
